prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System(CBTC): underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering-hours; protection overrides regulation; cybersecurity/trusted-communications prerequisite to automatic movement. Operations Control Centre’s Line Traffic Controller owns recovery/incidents/regulation; declares degradation for untrusted authority/location/points/platform/radio. Recovery requires independently/verbal-confirmed positions; automatic return requires stable/trusted communications, verified routes/positions, recorded maintenance-to-operations handback. Reset affecting routes/occupancy requires controller/Signal Maintenance Engineer(Maple) concurrence. Engineer verifies points/vacancy/protection before manual routes; read-only absent approved intervention; Axle Counter Reset Request controls failed-section restoration after occupancy checks. East Junction Interlocking(Falcon) supplies request, proves routes/points/releases, holds commanded points until field/verified-diagnostic safe-release confirmation; no locked/approach reset. West Junction Interlocking supplies Route Release Exception List; rejects manual-protection conflicts. North District Zone Controller(Marble)/South District Zone Controller(Orchid) validate authority/separation/locking; transfers require odometry/validation/reissue; North validates degraded-map limits before Temporary Speed Restriction Notice; South inhibits automatic routing in manually-confirmed-occupancy blocks. Atlas Onboard Controller(Kestrel): initialization/protected-manual/automatic-train-operation/fallback/cutout; enforces authority/speed/doors/braking; reports/stores faults/checksums/readiness. Missing authority/uncertain location requires restricted-manual; Dual Channel Odometer supplies distance/speed-plausibility; excessive disagreement invalidates location. Train Radio Modem reports connectivity-loss onboard; cab exposes intermittency. Wayside Radio Access Network failure requires throughput reduction before extended manual-working. Voice Dispatch Console authorizes restricted movements unless formal contingency; Revenue Train Operator reports hazards, repeats limits/speed/stopping/platform-clearance instructions, sends Test Train Clearance Memo after restricted-manual proving. Platform Screen Door Controller stays protected-local if stopping accuracy unverified. Metro Operations Control System(Lantern) sends Crew Login Token Bundle; distinguishes commanded/locked/occupied; preserves safety-alarm visibility. Service Timetable Server supplies approved context. Passenger Information Gateway receives reconciled predictions/stopping-pattern/platform-updates; issues controller-consistent disruptions; closed platforms unavailable. Maintenance Diagnostic Server(Quarry) retains events/notes/integrity, compares Brake Curve Checksum Log, incident-tags sessions before restart; incident-evidence frozen/protected/investigation-only. Cyber Security Officer reviews

New part:
S202: The Cyber Security Officer shall maintain continuous monitoring of security events from the Safety Data Communication Network, the Wayside Radio Access Network, and the Metro Operations Control System.
S203: Security monitoring shall correlate authentication failures, session resets, rejected messages, configuration changes, and abnormal timing patterns without altering any safety command path.
S204: Alerts affecting train control availability shall be classified using operational impact, affected territory, and whether the event could change train movement authority.
S205: The Line Traffic Controller shall be notified when a cybersecurity event requires a restriction on automatic operation or a change in communications mode.
S206: The Cyber Security Officer uses the audit file to investigate radio session continuity and to confirm that security monitoring records are complete.
S207: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance shall be the controlled source for operational certificates used by trainborne, wayside, control center, and maintenance components.
S208: Certificate issuance shall require approved asset identity, recorded software baseline, assigned operating domain, and confirmation that the requesting component is authorized for service.
S209: Certificate renewal shall be planned before expiry so that the Atlas Onboard Controller, Train Radio Modem, North District Zone Controller, South District Zone Controller, and West Junction Interlocking do not enter service with degraded trust.
S210: Falcon shall reject any control message with an invalid signature, an expired certificate, or a sequence value outside the accepted window.
S211: Revocation shall be available for a compromised device, a retired device, or a device whose maintenance history can no longer be reconciled with approved configuration records.
S212: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server shall not be used to bypass certificate checks or to create alternate trust paths into safety-related communications.
S213: Administrative access to the Cryptographic Key Management Appliance shall require named accounts, multifactor authentication, separation of duties, and recorded approval for privileged changes.
S214: The Signal Maintenance Engineer may request access needed for fault isolation, but the Cyber Security Officer shall approve security-sensitive permissions before they are enabled.
S215: The Revenue Train Operator shall not be assigned cybersecurity administration duties during passenger service, although security warnings presented in the cab shall remain part of normal operating awareness.
S216: The Metro Operations Control System uses the Test Train Clearance Memo as a controlled prerequisite before accepting security exceptions for non-revenue movement in protected territory.
S217: Audit evidence shall include time-synchronized event records, access approvals, certificate actions, configuration changes, alarm acknowledgements, and operator instructions related to communications security.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
